title: The Uncharted Landfall
premise: Sable Winterbourne, a bush pilot who has spent a decade ferrying medicine and gossip across the northern interior, is hired to search for a vanished government survey team. He finds them alive but changed: they have uncovered a rich ore deposit the government intends to seize from the Indigenous community that has lived beside it for generations, and one surveyor has stayed behind to destroy the evidence. Sable must choose between delivering the team home as ordered and helping expose what they found, knowing either choice makes him a target. In the end he flies the last surveyor's testimony to a journalist in Whitehorse, burns his own flight logs, and accepts exile from the skies he loved, finding that justice sometimes costs the very freedom it was meant to protect.
about_author: Elodie Brightwater is the pen name of a former northern bush pilot who logged over four thousand hours above the tree line before turning to fiction. She writes from a cabin outside Whitehorse, where the nearest neighbor is a floatplane base and the stories are all true, more or less.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine supply run over the Mackenzie basin establishes his world: the plane, the scattered outposts, his careful anonymity. He delivers medicine to a dying elder and overhears the first rumor of a survey team gone quiet. Emotional beat: the comfort of a life measured in distance, subtly fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A government man named Corliss offers triple his usual rate to fly a search pattern over the Kettle River plateau, where six surveyors missed their radio check-in for nine days. Sable hesitates; Corliss's paperwork has too many blanks. Emotional beat: suspicion warring with the debt he owes on his plane.

chapters.title: Empty Coordinates
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Three days of grid searches reveal nothing but a cache of gear left in unnervingly good order—rifles, tents, a radio with its antenna neatly coiled. No tracks lead out. Emotional beat: the creeping wrongness of a disappearance that looks less like disaster and more like intention.

chapters.title: The Woman at Windy Point
chapters.summary: Alternate POV: Mara Quill, the survey team's geologist, watching Sable's plane from a ridge, torn between signaling and staying hidden. Through her we learn the team didn't vanish—they scattered, after finding something in the core samples that made their leader radio Ottawa in a panic. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Plateau
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He spots a cookfire where no one should be, lands against his better judgment, and finds two surveyors half-starved, refusing to say why they walked away from their own camp. They beg him to fly them out and then, at the last moment, refuse to board. Emotional beat: the first crack in his neutrality.

chapters.title: What the Core Said
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flashback woven into present: the survey's discovery of a massive copper deposit directly beneath the Kettle River community's treaty land, and the order from Ottawa to falsify the boundaries. The team split—some took hush money, some ran, their leader Voss went silent. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Silence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He tracks Voss to an abandoned trapper's cabin and finds the man feverish with a broken ankle, guarding a satchel of core samples like a relic. Voss, delirious, makes Sable swear the samples will reach the Kettle River elders if he dies. Emotional beat: an oath given too easily, to be paid for dearly.

chapters.title: Corliss Returns
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Back at the strip, Corliss is waiting with new orders: fly the surveyors' coordinates to a mining company charter, forget the rest, and the debt on the plane disappears. He mentions, casually, that he knows about the satchel. Emotional beat: the trap closing with a smile.

chapters.title: The Weight of Cargo
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She comes down from the ridge to find Sable, testing him with half-truths before revealing the falsified survey maps. She needs his plane and his silence. He realizes she's been one step ahead of him since chapter one. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Fuel and Fire
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Someone torches his fuel cache at the strip. He suspects Corliss's men; the evidence points instead to one of the bought-off surveyors, Halloran, covering his own tracks. Sable is now grounded, broke, and the only pilot who knows the whole shape of the story. Emotional beat: isolation hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: The Kettle River Elders
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sable flies Voss and the samples to the Kettle River community on a borrowed fuel drum, where elder Josephine Cardinal reads the falsified maps and recognizes her grandfather's trapline redrawn into 'unoccupied' land. She asks Sable the question that guts him: whose side is he on when it costs him? Emotional beat: the personal made political.

chapters.title: Halloran's Confession
chapters.summary: Halloran's POV, brief and raw. The bought surveyor, drowning in drink and guilt, intercepts Sable to confess the bribe, the forged boundaries, and the fact that Corliss's charter isn't a mining company—it's enforcement, and they've been authorized to make the survey team's disappearance permanent. Emotional beat: cowardice finding its last shred of courage.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corliss's men take Voss and the satchel while Sable sleeps; Mara disappears into the bush after them. Sable faces his choice plainly: fly out, report nothing, survive. Instead he pulls his plane's engine apart to look busy while planning theft of his own aircraft back from Corliss's impound. Emotional beat: the pilot choosing to burn his own escape route.

chapters.title: Grand Theft, Cessna 180
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A tense, almost comic night sequence: Sable steals his own plane from a guarded impound at the Fort Providence strip, with Halloran drunk in the back seat insisting he can still navigate. They lift off with a searchlight sweeping the field. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration fused—the first time in ten years Sable has flown for something instead of away from it.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A storm forces them down on a frozen lake; a cracked strut means no more flying until repairs. In the tent, Halloran sobers up enough to give Sable the names and dates of the bribery chain, which Sable writes into his flight log—the one document he'd always kept honest. Emotional beat: the log becomes testimony; the miles become evidence.

chapters.title: What Voss Carried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara catches up to Corliss's convoy on foot and finds Voss alive but beaten, the satchel already opened—Corliss has the samples but not the field notebooks, which Voss hid in the one place no one would look: the survey team's official report, filed and sealed in Yellowknife. Emotional beat: hope hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Sealed Report
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sable flies Mara to Yellowknife through a corridor of bad weather, dodging a company charter that shadows them. They break into the survey office to photograph the original notebooks before Corliss's men can intercept the seal. Emotional beat: two people who trusted no one learning to work in tandem.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Float Base
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The mechanic who lent Sable fuel sells him out; Corliss's men take Mara and the photographs at the dock. Corliss offers Sable his final bargain: fly one last run for the company and everyone walks away, including the Kettle River community, who will simply never know what was taken. Emotional beat: the corruption of power shown as an offer, not a threat.

chapters.title: The Answer Is No
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable stalls, then leads Corliss's charter on a chase into a box canyon where the company plane, heavier and faster, cannot follow—a pilot's duel decided by knowledge of the land, not machinery. He lands at Kettle River as the community, warned by Josephine, stands armed and unmovable at the strip. Emotional beat: the land itself taking a side.

chapters.title: Climax: The Hearing on the Tarmac
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. A federal investigator, tipped by Halloran's sworn statement, arrives by chance and by design; Corliss attempts one last seizure of the evidence and is undone by his own pilot, who defects with the company's radio records. Voss, carried on a stretcher, identifies the falsified maps in front of everyone. Emotional beat: justice arriving not through courts but through witnesses refusing to stay silent.

chapters.title: After the Noise
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The inquiry begins; the Kettle River boundaries are redrawn; Voss recovers; Mara takes a post defending the community's claim. Sable's stolen-aircraft charge is quietly dropped, but Corliss's employers remember his face. He is offered a safe route back to invisibility and declines it. Emotional beat: grief for the anonymous life, and relief at its loss.

chapters.title: The Uncharted Landfall
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, final flight. Sable flies the medicine run one more time, then lands at Kettle River for good, trading the cockpit for a ground loop he can walk: hauling supplies by boat and trail for the community, Mara beside him. He measures life in years now. Emotional beat: landing at last—not escaping the map, but choosing where to stand on it.
